nasa-tm-19680000663-review-of-nondestruc:
John A. Gibson, of the Battelle Memorial Institute in Columbus, Ohio, reviewed weld inspection methods in October 1967. The flaw in question is lack of penetration: a fusion weld that fails to join through the full thickness. His review covers butt joints in aluminum alloys welded from both sides.

A literature search tested how well standard methods find that flaw. Under some conditions, Gibson reports, ordinary ultrasonic and X-ray inspection may miss it. He reviews two improved X-ray approaches, including measuring density changes across the weld. Two ultrasonic upgrades also appear, one raising the test frequency. Some approaches plant an easy-to-see flaw that vanishes when penetration is complete.
